I'm not arguing against Solid, I'm just saying it's not going to really do much for the real issue of data privacy for most people.

Why?

Solid provides a way to link pieces of data which live on different devices, servers, platforms, etc. It decouples the storage of data from the applications using it, give you control over what apps get access to what data.

This doesn't addresses the real issue of protecting and auditing what happens with your data when you do share it with those apps. It doesn't keep those apps from sharing it with 3rd parties, aggregating it, abusing it, storing it on their own servers which are susceptible to hacking, etc.

This could actually make it easier for 3rd parties to aggregate data on people. Yes, you'd have to grant that sharing for it to occur with Solid, but there's still nothing stopping these 3rd parties from sharing data through back channels like they do now and again, there's nothing protecting what happens with your data once you do share it with some 3rd party.

Also, in your scenario of doing a data backup, this doesn't automatically mean your backups won't reside on some 3rd party server.

Solid simply decouples your data from apps and lets you decide where it resides. If you want geographically diverse redundancy of your data, you're still going to have to use some 3rd party service or run your own servers like you do today.
